delivering a superior connectivity, differentiated offerings, and a seamless service proposition. We are investing in fiber home pass

agenda is anchored on three priorities. First, is to strengthen our infrastructure backbone to meet the demanding needs of enterprise
customers. This includes sustained investments in network quality, reliability, and resilience, with a clear focus on delivering a world-
class B2B network. Second is sharpening our offerings around customer needs across industries and segments, building capabilities

customer relationships and a larger share of wallet. And third, is strengthening our delivery and service assurance through digital
platforms and AI. The focus is on disciplined delivery, automated root cause analysis, and proactive fault resolution to deliver
consistently superior customer experience. These priorities underpin our ambition to capture a larger share of the enterprise
opportunity and drive sustained growth across our portfolio.
Moving on to the second pillar of our strategy, which is obsession to deliver brilliant customer experience. Customer experience
underpins everything we do, from how we invest in our networks to how we design our digital journeys. On the network, we are building
for quality and resilience, we are strengthening a transport layer beneath the 5G network and building edge data centers that make
the network more resilient. Capabilities such as Fast Lane built on 5G network slicing add a differentiated experience where customers
need it most in busy networks. In homes, our focus is on getting the fundamentals right across installation, service, and workmanship.
Our AI-led workmanship tools running on the field engineer's own handset are helping standardize the quality of our execution on
ground. Underpinning all of this is our unified customer data platform, which brings the customer’s journey across channels and
touchpoints into a single view. At the core is our Converge Data Engine, which combines data, AI, and analytics to bring real-time
context to every interaction, anticipating customer needs and delivering a personalized experience at scale. The result is a simpler,
more relevant interaction, and a deeper relationship with our customers.
The third pillar of our strategy is to build and leverage our digital capabilities. AI is increasingly woven into the fabric of our business.
Over the past two quarters, we have laid the foundation to embed AI at the heart of Airtel’s digital platforms. We have built a homegrown
agent platform called Agent Bridge and added GPU capacity across our data centers. This is enabling us to activate AI use cases
much faster across both customer-facing and internal journeys. In parallel, we have run several AI experiments to reimagine our
operating models with an intent to redesign how work gets done at Airtel. Going forward, our focus is on scaling the use cases already
creating strong value.
Let me share a few highlights. For customers, our real-time, context-led decision engine has now generated over 10 billion next best
actions and is scaled across key inventories across our channels. We use individual-level context to deliver more than a billion
personalized content and recommendations. Since launch, our AI-led anti-spam solution has identified over 100 billion calls for spam,
and nearly 5 billion messages, and blocked over 1.7 million fraudulent links. For networks, AI is helping us lower our fuel and power
wastage, which reduces operating costs while also improving customer experience. Our AI-enabled RAM dynamically orchestrated
over 14 million sleep hours each day across our network sites during Q2, reducing energy consumption and generating some cost
savings. We see substantial headroom to further optimize our energy costs as these capabilities scale across the network. The third
area is internal functions where AI tools are now changing the way our internal processes are. Call center bots were the early use
case we adopted. Now, AI-led processes are changing across areas like quarterly financial book closure, recruitment, mass interview
screening of candidates, and our video KYCs for our customer acquisition. As we scale AI across Airtel, we are also remaining focused
on clear guardrails around customer safety, privacy, and data sovereignty.
The fourth pillar of our strategy is War on Waste. Cost discipline remains core to how we operate and as cost pressures build, funding
the growth will depend on how much waste we take out of the system. The War on Waste initiative continues. We are also looking
beyond efficiency towards innovation that changes the cost equation itself, in areas like energy and in virtualizing set-up boxes for
IPTV, for example. These initiatives are helping us mitigate inflationary pressures arising from ongoing geopolitical headwinds.
So, to sum up. Overall, we have delivered another quarter of strong performance, underpinned by our portfolio premiumization, razor-
sharp execution, and sustained operational excellence. We remain confident in the growth potential across our businesses, supported
by continued ARPU expansion in mobility, deeper penetration of homes, and the increasing scale of our B2B portfolio. Our investments
are channelized towards future-proofing Airtel. AI is now becoming integral to the way we work, enabling us to enhance productivity
and improve agility. At the core of all these investments and initiatives is a relentless focus on delivering superior customer experience.
With that, let me hand this back over to Vaidehi for the Q&A session.
